title: Precedent and architectural reinterpretation
question: How were ancient and earlier domed precedents selectively reinterpreted in Renaissance and later European architecture, and which connections are documented rather than inferred from visual resemblance?
selection_rationale: The five Features form a discontinuous sequence from Roman precedent through Renaissance construction and centralized planning to a later national monument. The set was chosen because it supports two explicit derivation claims and two documented limiters instead of treating every dome as one influence chain.

features.name: Pantheon (Rome)
features.selection_rationale: Provides the ancient centralized domed precedent explicitly named by the Villa Rotonda evidence and used as a limiting comparison for St. Peter's.

features.name: Brunelleschi’s Dome (Florence Cathedral)
features.selection_rationale: Separates documented construction innovation from unsupported assumptions that every later masonry dome derives directly from the Pantheon.

features.name: St. Peter's Basilica
features.selection_rationale: Supplies the explicitly cited dome model for Soufflot and a contested scholarly comparison with the Pantheon.

features.name: Villa Almerico Capra “La Rotonda”
features.selection_rationale: Offers an official, unusually explicit statement of derivation from the Pantheon together with evidence that the executed dome differs from Palladio's published design.

features.name: Panthéon (Paris)
features.selection_rationale: Provides a later documented act of modelling and competitive ambition directed toward St. Peter's rather than a generic classical resemblance.

claims.statement: The Hadrianic Pantheon's unreinforced dome has a 43.30-metre diameter equal to its interior height.
claims.uncertainty: The official record gives the principal geometry but does not provide a full structural analysis.

claims.statement: Brunelleschi's dome was constructed as an octagonal, double-shell masonry structure without timber reinforcement.
claims.uncertainty: The source describes the executed system but does not establish a direct historical relation to any other selected Feature.

claims.statement: La Rotonda organizes its cubic volume around a central circular domed room.
claims.uncertainty: This formal description alone does not prove derivation.

claims.statement: The official Villa Rotonda history states that its circular domed conception derives from the Pantheon in Rome.
claims.uncertainty: The source supports conceptual derivation but does not claim literal copying of the Pantheon's structure.

relation.qualifier: central circular domed conception, not a wholesale structural copy

claims.statement: The official villa history distinguishes Palladio's published hemispherical dome from Vincenzo Scamozzi's lower executed dome.
claims.uncertainty: The official page does not fully separate Palladio's design decisions from Scamozzi's execution decisions.

claims.statement: St. Peter's dome was executed as a double shell with an ogival outer profile.
claims.uncertainty: The concise official page does not assign every design alteration among the successive architects.

claims.statement: Soufflot modelled aspects of Sainte-Geneviève, especially its dome, on St. Peter's Basilica.
claims.uncertainty: The same study names St. Paul's and Les Invalides as additional models, so St. Peter's was not an exclusive source.

relation.qualifier: selected aspects, especially the dome, alongside other church models

claims.statement: Ian Campbell argues that the as-built dome of St. Peter's has little formal similarity to the Pantheon apart from size.
claims.uncertainty: This is a scholarly interpretation within a broader symbolic argument, not a measured comparative survey.

claims.statement: Paolo Almerico commissioned La Rotonda to combine residential and representational duties.
claims.uncertainty: The official villa narrative summarizes the commission but does not reproduce the complete patronage archive.

claims.statement: In 1791, the former church of Sainte-Geneviève became a national necropolis.
claims.uncertainty: The building changed between religious and secular uses several more times during the nineteenth century.

evidence_links.evidence_summary: The page distinguishes Palladio's drawn hemisphere from Scamozzi's executed, lower dome and locates the Pantheon resemblance in the latter.

evidence_links.evidence_summary: The article explicitly names St. Peter's, especially Michelangelo's dome, among three models for Sainte-Geneviève.
The monument authority records Soufflot's ambition to compete with St. Peter's and St. Paul's.

evidence_links.evidence_summary: Campbell frames a symbolic Pantheon association and then limits the as-built formal resemblance to size.

evidence_links.locator: English version, paragraph 2 beginning “The present building”
evidence_links.evidence_summary: The Pantheon's documented geometry provides the institutional baseline for the size comparison without proving transmission.

evidence_links.evidence_summary: The villa history separately describes Almerico's residential and representative requirements for the commission.

evidence_links.evidence_summary: The monument authority links Louis XV's vow and reconstruction promise to the 1791 conversion into a national necropolis.

conclusion.statement: The module supports two selective, source-named acts of derivation: La Rotonda from the Pantheon's centralized domed conception and Soufflot's Panthéon from aspects of St. Peter's. It does not support a continuous Pantheon-to-Florence-to-St. Peter's-to-Paris genealogy; construction, execution history and competing models interrupt that shortcut.

module_uncertainty: The package does not claim that every formal resemblance among the five domes records transmission.
The attribution boundary between Palladio's design and Scamozzi's executed dome requires specialist review.
The Campbell interpretation should be checked against additional St. Peter's scholarship before external validation.
Claims and EvidenceLinks remain draft until both independent reviewers confirm the corrected frozen revision.
